findings.note: Oilers team site, Nov 20: Nugent-Hopkins missed Friday's practice and may miss a fourth straight game, while Edmonton finishes a six-game road trip with a back-to-back and three games in four days. Carolina looks fully healthy.

ESPN's game page shows Carolina averaging 33.0 shots for and 21.6 against, versus Edmonton's 24.8 and 26.4. Kochetkov has a .920 save percentage, compared with .906 for Levi and .912 for Jarry. Andersen is on IR.

Jonathan Davis of VSiN bets a half unit on the Oilers moneyline at +150. He notes that Edmonton won the October meeting 6-5 in a shootout and that McDavid has a nine-game point streak against Carolina.

ESPN's game page shows Carolina allowing 2.18 goals and 21.6 shots per game, and its likely starter Pyotr Kochetkov has a 1.64 GAA and .920 save percentage, which makes this a tough matchup for a 2+ point game.

The Oilers' pre-game report says McDavid's 23-game point streak ended Thursday against Tampa Bay, Filip Hallander is filling in on his line while Nugent-Hopkins is out, and this game opens a back-to-back during a stretch of three games in four days.
VSiN's Jonathan Davis picks McDavid for 2+ points at +115 for 1 unit, pointing to McDavid's nine-game point streak against Carolina, with 2+ points in six of those games.

NHL.com lists Bedard (shoulder) and Byram as out for Chicago and says Commesso could make his season debut here or Sunday. Wolf is expected to start a third straight game for Calgary, and Backlund, Pospisil and Middleton did not skate at Friday's optional practice.

Chicago is 6-14-2 and 0-8-1 on the road; Calgary is only 10-12-1 (6-6-0 at home), lost 4-1 to Minnesota Thursday, and has Zary and Huberdeau out. Likely starter Wolf has a .878 save percentage, below Cooley's .906.

CBS shows Calgary at -164 and Chicago at +137 with a 5.5 total, so the -160 offered is about the market price. Calgary's goal scoring (2.47 per game) is nearly the same as Chicago's (2.43), and no expert pick was visible.

NHL.com's projected lineups list Ryan O'Reilly as Nashville's first-line center, but he left practice early Friday and there was no update on his status. The same page says Pittsburgh's Malkin isn't traveling and Rust, Robertson, Graves and Soderblom are injured.

ESPN lists Nashville at 11-6-5 (6-3-2 at home) and Pittsburgh at 7-11-2 (3-7-1 away). Saros has a .918 save percentage, while Pittsburgh's goalies are at .873 and .894. Pittsburgh won the first meeting this season 3-2.

Covers' odds comparison now shows BetMGM at -145 for Nashville, versus the -135 being offered, with other books between -130 and -145. That suggests the market moved toward Nashville, or the -135 price may be stale.
